task_title: Declare a table over HTTP and publish declaration adoption on /metrics
task_criteria: POST /api/ns/:ns/tables/:table/declare writes a declaration through the SAME core as the CLI verb and the MCP tool (declareTable in src/tables/declare.ts), returning the resulting declaration, and an unauthenticated/grant-restricted caller cannot use it (namespace + per-table write grant).
An end-to-end run on a scratch daemon proves an HTTP client can declare a table and immediately insert and read a row, with a pre-fix control (origin/main tree) answering 404 for the same request.

Declaration adoption is a number on the scrape surface: duckbrain_table_declaration_namespaces{format=schema.json|legacy} and duckbrain_table_declarations{format} are sampled from the namespaces root at collect time, emit NO sample when there is no store, and move when a namespace adopts schema.json.

The legacy-vs-schema.json shape decision is recorded in docs (why a partial migration is worse than none, what legacy costs, the per-table recipe with rollback), and the docs name the one path a user should take.
The full suite is green and test-counts.json is bumped in the same commit.

tier2.summary:
COMPLETE
  ✓ POST /api/ns/:ns/tables/:table/declare writes a declaration through the SAME core as the CLI verb and the MCP tool (declareTable in src/tables/declare.ts), returning the resulting declaration, and an unauthenticated/grant-restricted caller cannot use it (namespace + per-table write grant).: src/http/routes/tables.ts:1076-1110 registers router.post("/:table/declare") with requireNamespaceGrant((req)=>param(req,"ns")) and requireTableGrant(grantNs, grantTable, "write") (lines 1079-1080), parses the body via parseDeclarationBody (lines 158-240, rejects unknown keys) and calls declareTable(spec) imported from src/tables/declare.ts (line 106) — the same core used by src/cli/tables.ts:243 and src/mcp/tools/tables.ts:206. Response returns namespace/table/path/format/replacedExisting plus the resolved declaration (resolveTableDeclaration) with 201 new / 200 replaced. Tests src/http/routes/tables-declare-adopt001.test.ts assert 201+declaration, insert+read, 409 conflict, and authz: 403 FORBIDDEN "no write grant for table 'new_table'" with nothing written to schema.json, granted table 201. Full suite green (268 files / 2261 tests). [resolution 0.16; src/tables/declare.ts]
  ✓ An end-to-end run on a scratch daemon proves an HTTP client can declare a table and immediately insert and read a row, with a pre-fix control (origin/main tree) answering 404 for the same request.: scripts/proofs/adopt-declared-001.sh boots the real CLI (node bin/duckbrain.js http) on scratch ports 28771-28773 with scratch namespaces roots; section 1 does declare→201 schema.json, insert→201, GET→200 with the row, and /metrics gauge check; section 3 creates a detached worktree of the pre-fix ref (default d0264bd4^) and asserts 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND. Verified statically that the pre-fix tree (d0264bd4^:src/http/routes/tables.ts) has no /:table/declare route (only POST /_transaction and POST /:table) and that src/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts:163-172 emits 404 code ROUTE_NOT_FOUND, so the control is sound. Transcript recorded in docs/evidence/adopt-declared-001-2026-11-06.md (declare 201, insert 201, GET 200, gauges schema.json 1/legacy 0, 401/403/201 authz, pre-fix 404). I did not re-execute the proof script (requires pnpm install in a worktree and daemon boots); evidence is the committed transcript plus code inspection.
  ✓ Declaration adoption is a number on the scrape surface: duckbrain_table_declaration_namespaces{format=schema.json|legacy} and duckbrain_table_declarations{format} are sampled from the namespaces root at collect time, emit NO sample when there is no store, and move when a namespace adopts schema.json.: src/metrics/declarations.ts measureDeclarations() walks the namespaces root counting schema.json vs tables/*.table.json per namespace; createDeclarationSampler is TTL(60s)+single-flight. src/http/metrics.ts:643-711 builds the sampler only when namespacesPath is set (wired from src/cli/http.ts:577-588 namespacesPath = resolveNamespacesPath()), and registers Gauge DECLARATION_NAMESPACES / DECLARATION_TABLES with labelNames ["format"] and collect: publishDeclarations — collect-time sampling, no timer. publishDeclarations (lines 657-695) calls withdraw() (gauge.remove for both formats) when there is no sampler or no census, so no sample is emitted without a store. Tests src/metrics/declarations-adopt001.test.ts cover both shapes, the adoption move (schema.json 0→1 after a namespace adopts), and "emits no adoption series for an embedder that declared no store"; src/http/metrics.test.ts:168-171 asserts both families in the exposition. Suite green: `npx vitest run --reporter=dot` → Test Files 268 passed (268), Tests 2261 passed (2261). [resolution 0.16; schema.json]
  ✓ The legacy-vs-schema.json shape decision is recorded in docs (why a partial migration is worse than none, what legacy costs, the per-table recipe with rollback), and the docs name the one path a user should take.: docs/decisions/ADOPT-DECLARED-001-declaration-shape.md contains: "Why a partial migration is worse than none" (legacy always wins on a name conflict per src/schema/table-registry.ts, so the switch happens at the legacy-file delete), "What the legacy shape costs (sourced)" table (no DB-SUPA-5 change record, no SUPA-2 barrier, no relations/embed, no composite keyColumns/views, silent collision), a 5-step per-table migration recipe with step 5 rollback ("restore the deleted legacy file — legacy wins again"), and a Decision section naming the one path: "New tables declare schema.json". Reinforced in docs/api/http-api.md (declare route, one implementation) and docs/guide/cli-reference.md ("Declare NEW tables without --legacy"). [resolution 0.16; legacy-vs-schema.json]
  ✓ The full suite is green and test-counts.json is bumped in the same commit.: Ran `npx vitest run --reporter=dot` in the working tree: exit 0, output "Test Files  268 passed (268)" and "Tests  2261 passed (2261)". test-counts.json now reads {"suites": 268, "tests": 2261}, and commit d0264bd4 bumps it from 266/2248 → 268/2261 in the same commit that adds src/http/routes/tables-declare-adopt001.test.ts and src/metrics/declarations-adopt001.test.ts (git show d0264bd4 -- test-counts.json). [resolution 0.16; test-counts.json]
